Team —

Quick ask to clean up the Q2 forecast in SFDC so finance has an accurate commit number by COB Friday. I pulled a snapshot and there are a few patterns driving noise: stale close dates, opportunities sitting in "Proposal" >60 days with no activity, and several "Commit" stage opps without updated next-step notes.

Please do the following by EOD Friday (2026-03-13):
- Push close dates on any opps not expected to close this quarter (set new expected close or move to next quarter).
- Move to "Risk"/"Upside" if you can no longer commit — only true commits should be in the Commit stage.
- Add a one-line next-step note for each Commit opp (who’s involved, next milestone, probability confirmation).
- Archive any opps with no contact/activity >120 days and no planned engagement (use the stale-opps list to triage).

I've attached a snapshot and a CSV of flagged stale opps. Use the spreadsheet to prioritize. If you think something on the Commit list should remain, call it out with a 1-line justification in the spreadsheet.

Attachments: [Attachment: Q2_pipeline_snapshot.xlsx (Excel, 110KB)] [Attachment: stale-opps-list.csv (CSV, 8KB)]

Why this matters: finance will use SFDC Commit to size Q2 cash flow and our Dedicated capacity plan — overcommitment means we’ll either overprovision GPU pools or face surprises on margins. Simple hygiene now saves headache later.

If you need clarifications on the commit definition: commit = verbal agreement + mutually agreed timeline + customer contact committed to purchase this quarter. If any of those are missing, the correct action is to move to Upside or update the close date.

Thanks — please reply in thread if you’ve completed your refresh so I can summarize for FP&A.

—Marissa
